newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Third Red Terror trial opens in Addis Ababa.
newsitem.headline: Third Red Terror trial opens in Addis Ababa.

text.p: The trial of 32 people charged with genocide and murder during the 1970s Red Terror campaign in Ethiopia began on Friday, the third such trial to open this week.
Only 23 of the accused appeared in court in Addis Ababa on Friday. The other nine were charged in absentia.
Other trials started on Monday and Wednesday of 173 people including Olympic marathon gold medallist Mamo Wolde.
The 32 who appeared in court on Friday were charged with causing bodily harm through torture and executing members of the opposition without due process of the law between 1975 and 1979.
All the defendants were charged under the Ethiopian Penal Code of 1957 and face the death penalty if found guilty.

"The accused who had served as revolutionary guards and members of Red Terror committees, acting in groups at different times, took prisoners from different detention centres in District 25 (in Addis Ababa) around midnight -- executed them and then dumped their bodies along road sides and under bridges," the charge sheet stated.

The accused were charged with serving as a group to eliminate political opponents of the Dergue, the Marxist military junta of deposed leader Mengistu Haile Mariam which seized power in Ethiopia in 1974 and was toppled in 1991.
They were also accused of executing political opponents and leaving their bodies on roadsides in the capital and inflicting torture and bodily harm on groups of political opponents.
Friday's trial was adjourned until May 30 to allow the defendants time to find defence lawyers.
The government has charged a total of 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide. Of these 1,200 are suspected of involvement in the Red Terror under Mengistu.

Mengistu fled after being ousted in May 1991 and lives in exile in Zimbabwe. He is among 25 former Dergue officials being tried in absentia in Addis Ababa accused of genocide and crimes against humanity.
